cards.text: Samuel, the prophet who anointed Saul king, has a message for him: “Now therefore, listen to the words of the LORD.” The LORD of Hosts says He saw what the Amalekites did when they opposed Israel on the way up from Egypt. And now He's sending Saul on a mission.

cards.question: The LORD's command is about the Amalekites and everything that belongs to them. What does He tell Saul to do with all of it?

answers.text: Take the best of it as plunder

cards.question: True or false: The LORD tells Saul he can keep the Amalekites' oxen and sheep.

cards.text: Saul calls up the troops and counts them at Telaim: 200,000 foot soldiers and 10,000 men of Judah. TWO HUNDRED TEN THOUSAND, friend, and I spent years in a junk drawer counting the dust and never got past forty.
Saul comes to the city of Amalek and lies in wait in the valley. Then he sends a warning to the Kenites: get away from the Amalekites.

cards.question: Saul warns the Kenites so they don't get swept away with the Amalekites. Why does he spare them?

answers.text: They were kind to Israel leaving Egypt
They paid Saul to protect them
They promised to fight for Saul

cards.question: True or false: The Kenites ignore Saul's warning and stay near the Amalekites.

cards.text: Then Saul strikes down the Amalekites all the way from Havilah to Shur, which is east of Egypt.

cards.question: In the battle, Saul captures one Amalekite alive. Who is it?

cards.text: And Agag isn't the only thing Saul and his troops spare. They look over the flocks and herds like it's the last tray of cookies on the cooling rack.

cards.question: Saul and his troops spare the ___ of the sheep and cattle.
Saul and his troops are unwilling to destroy the best. So what do they devote to destruction?

cards.text: Then the word of the LORD comes to Samuel.

cards.question: The LORD tells Samuel: “I ___ that I have made Saul king, for he has turned away from following Me and has not carried out My instructions.”
Samuel hears that Saul has turned away from following the LORD. What does Samuel do?

answers.text: Cries out to the LORD all night
Calls the elders together that night
Writes Saul a warning that night

cards.text: Early in the morning, Samuel gets up to go confront Saul. But someone tells him Saul's gone to Carmel, and he's set something up there.

cards.question: What has Saul set up at Carmel?

cards.text: Then Saul's turned and gone down to Gilgal, so that's where Samuel catches up with him. Saul greets him: “May the LORD bless you.”

cards.question: Right after greeting Samuel, what does Saul tell him?

answers.text: He carried out the LORD's instructions
He needs help dividing the plunder
His troops refused to finish the job

cards.question: Saul says the job's done. Then Samuel asks him about a sound he hears. What is it?

cards.text: Friend, the man says MISSION COMPLETE while the evidence is MOOING behind him. That's me back in the Millers' kitchen, swearing I never touched the dough with flour all over my mustache.

cards.question: Saul has an answer for the animals. Who does he say brought them from the Amalekites?
What does Saul say the best sheep and cattle were spared for?

cards.text: “Stop!” Samuel says. “Let me tell you what the LORD said to me last night.” And Saul says, “Tell me.”
Samuel reminds Saul that he was once small in his own eyes, and now he's the head of the tribes of Israel. The LORD anointed him king and sent him on a mission to wipe out the sinful Amalekites.

cards.question: Samuel asks Saul why he didn't obey the LORD: “Why did you rush upon the ___ and do evil in the sight of the LORD?”
True or false: When Samuel asks why he didn't obey, Saul admits right away that he disobeyed.

cards.text: “But I did obey the LORD,” Saul says. He brought back Agag and devoted the Amalekites to destruction, and he says the troops took the best of the plunder to sacrifice to the LORD at Gilgal.
He is STICKING to it, like the dead batteries I shared that junk drawer with, swearing they still had a little charge left.

cards.question: Saul keeps pointing to the sacrifices. Samuel says something is better than sacrifice. What is it?
True or false: Samuel says attentiveness is better than the fat of rams.

cards.text: Then Samuel says rebellion is like the sin of divination, and arrogance is like the wickedness of idolatry.

cards.question: Saul has rejected the word of the LORD. Because of that, what does Samuel say the LORD has done?

cards.text: Samuel has just told Saul the LORD rejected him as king. Now Saul finally says it: he has sinned and broken the LORD's commandment and Samuel's instructions. Took a whole lecture and a herd of mooing evidence, but he gets there.

cards.question: Saul tells Samuel why he disobeyed. What reason does he give?

answers.text: He feared the people and obeyed them
Agag offered him a peace treaty

cards.question: Then Saul asks Samuel for something. What does he ask?

answers.text: To forgive him and come back with him
To anoint him king a second time
To pray for the troops at Gilgal

cards.question: True or false: The first time Saul asks Samuel to come back with him, Samuel says yes.

cards.text: Samuel tells him again that the LORD has rejected him as king over Israel. As Samuel turns to go, Saul grabs the hem of his robe.

cards.question: Saul grabs the hem of Samuel's robe as Samuel turns to go. What happens to it?

answers.text: The hem slips from Saul's grip
The hem catches on the gate

cards.question: Samuel tells Saul the LORD has torn something from him today. What is it?
Who does Samuel say the LORD has given the kingdom of Israel to?

cards.text: Then Samuel says, “the Glory of Israel does not lie or change His mind, for He is not a man, that He should change His mind.”
“I have sinned,” Saul says. That line again, and then he asks Samuel for something in front of the elders and all Israel.

cards.question: What does Saul ask Samuel to do before the elders of his people and before Israel?

answers.text: Honor him in front of them
Bless the troops in front of them
Read the law in front of them

cards.question: True or false: This time Samuel goes back with Saul, and Saul worships the LORD.

cards.text: Then Samuel says, “Bring me Agag king of the Amalekites.” And Agag comes to him cheerfully.

cards.question: Agag walks up to Samuel cheerfully. What does he think?

answers.text: The danger of death is behind him
Samuel wants to make peace with Amalek
He is about to get his throne back

cards.text: But Samuel declares, “As your sword has made women childless, so your mother will be childless among women.” And Samuel hacks Agag to pieces before the LORD at Gilgal.

cards.question: After that, Samuel goes to Ramah. Where does Saul go?

answers.text: His home in Gibeah of Saul

cards.question: True or false: Samuel visits Saul again before Saul dies.

cards.text: Samuel mourns for Saul. And the LORD regrets that He made Saul king over Israel.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 14 quotes "I ___ that I have made Saul king, for he has turned away from following Me and has not carried out My instructions.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 11 quotes "Why did you rush upon the ___ and do evil in the sight of the LORD?", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card ends with "And now He's sending Saul on a mission," which comes from the LORD's command in 1 Samuel 15:3 ("Now go and attack the Amalekites"). The card cites only 1 Samuel 15:1-2.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The joke adds a new detail to the drawer backstory: Papa Dorin counted the dust and "never got past forty." The backstory only says they counted the dust as it fell. Jokes may make up small moments around his bakery, not new details about the drawer.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: "Then Saul strikes down the Amalekites all the way from Havilah to Shur, which is east of Egypt." This is a bare restatement of the verse with none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The question asks which Amalekite Saul captured alive. Only the right answer, "Agag king of Amalek," names Amalek. The other two, "Achish king of Gath" and "Og king of Bashan," are plainly not Amalekites. The setup rules them out and the right answer stands out.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This is the same issue under the answer rules. The right answer matches the question's word "Amalekite" and the wrong answers do not.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The core action in 1 Samuel 15:9 is keeping the best and destroying only the worthless. The comparison, looking over flocks "like it's the last tray of cookies on the cooling rack," shows eyeing something, not keeping the best and throwing out the rest. "Look over the flocks and herds" also adds an action the text doesn't give. The line is mild and doesn't land as a laugh.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: "Then the word of the LORD comes to Samuel." The card is stripped down and has no voice or context.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: This card is only a joke. It tells no new part of the passage and repeats the moment that card 5 just asked about.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The joke makes up a new backstory moment: Papa Dorin "swearing I never touched the dough" in the Millers' kitchen. It also doesn't make sense. He is a cookie stamper whose job is touching dough, and the backstory says the family stole dough, not him.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: A stamper denying he touched the dough is confusing, because touching dough is what stampers do. A stranger would say "huh?"

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: This card is only a joke (the dead batteries). It tells nothing new and repeats the citation of card 13, 1 Samuel 15:20-21. The joke should ride along on card 13 instead of standing alone.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences. Only the opening card of the walkthrough may have 3. It also restates 1 Samuel 15:23 ("Samuel has just told Saul the LORD rejected him as king") but cites only 15:24.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question says "This time Samuel goes back with Saul," but no card tells that Saul asks again in 1 Samuel 15:30 ("Come back with me, so that I may worship the LORD your God"). Cards 10 and 11 cover only the request for honor. The baker hasn't been told there is a second request to come back, so "This time" has no setup.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.
